title: K=4 strict-h0 CRRA REE contour-Phi: genuine PR fixed point hunt

k3_prior_evidence.note: K=3 plateau (flint_persist2) best ferr=1.2e-4 at deficit~0.27, d_FR~0.25; k3_plateau_table shows plateau_floor ~0.05-0.08 with deficit>0.2 across gamma. K=3 itself has NO genuine PR FP, only a non-smooth plateau.

verdict_test_A: TEST A (tau4->.. homotopy, heterogeneous tau): the tracked low-residual solution sits on the FR manifold (deficit ~0.001-0.002) at EVERY tau4 in {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2}; residual stays on the non-smooth floor (~1e-3..2e-2) and the accurate 1485-col Newton stalls (alpha->2e-4) without reaching a true FP floor. PR character merges into FR immediately above the degenerate tau4=0 limit (where this operator collapses to P==0.5). No PR branch persists. NO genuine K=4 PR FP via continuation.
verdict_test_B: TEST B (symmetric 495-dim, accurate-Jacobian Newton, genuinely-partial seeds): every seed floors on the non-smooth plateau, none reaches ||F||inf<1e-5. subset2 Finf=0.246/def=0.021; subset3 Finf=0.197/def=0.011; k3embed Finf=0.249/def=0.042; nl_symmetrized FROZEN at its initial Finf=0.430/def=0.218 (Newton step alpha->3e-8 immediately). The only deficit>0.05 point (nl, def=0.218) has the LARGEST residual (0.43) -- the hallmark of a non-smooth plateau, NOT a fixed point.
verdict: NO genuine K=4 partially-revealing fixed point exists (gamma=0.1, tau base 2, strict h0, G_inner=9). The ONLY true K=4 fixed point is the fully-revealing one (||F||inf=9.45e-6, deficit~0). Every partially-revealing surface is at best a NON-SMOOTH PLATEAU: deficit>0 but ||F||inf floored at ~0.07-0.43 (homogeneous) / ~1e-3..2e-2 (along the heterogeneous homotopy, where it additionally collapses to deficit~0/FR). Newton with an accurate Jacobian stalls on the floor at any deficit>0 and never reaches ~1e-5. This matches K=3 (PR only as a ~0.06-0.2 plateau, no true FP) and the homogeneous k4_sym result; consistent with PR requiring noise/smoothing. Conclusion (b): only FR is a genuine K=4 FP; PR is a plateau, not a fixed point.
note_best_pr_global_homotopy: test_A.best_pr_global (tau4=2, deficit=0.064, Finf=0.068) is a transient PR-region iterate seen during a Picard/Anderson sweep, NOT a fixed point: its residual 0.068 is the non-smooth floor, far above 1e-5. It does not survive Newton.
